# Pakistan

Values for an OG-Core calibration, then the estimates behind them. How to use them: [calibration guide](../calibration-guide.md).

## Values for OG-Core

| OG-Core input | Wealth gradient | Source |
|---|---|---|
| `fert_gradient` | −0.65, by age as below | DHS 2017, TFR, plus [age offsets](../methods/fertility-by-age.md) |
| `infmort_gradient` | −0.53 | DHS 2017, infant mortality rate |
| `mort_gradient` | −0.76 (95% prediction interval −1.45 to −0.07) | [general gradient](../methods/general-gradient.md) at GDP per capita (PPP, constant 2021 international $) of $5,617 (2025, World Bank) |
| `imm_pctiles` | not provided | — |

Divide each value by 100 × (1 − p) before passing it to OG-Core ([how](../calibration-guide.md#converting-a-gradient-to-og-cores-units)).

## Estimates

### Household surveys

Latest DHS or MICS survey for each indicator ([`gradient_library_latest.csv`](../../data/gradient_library_latest.csv)).

| Indicator | Survey | Lowest | Second | Middle | Fourth | Highest | Low/high ratio | Gradient |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Notes

- The 2006–07 DHS recorded deaths of household members in all sampled households, but household assets, and so the wealth index, only in the subsample that received the full questionnaire. That subsample holds fewer than 900 adult deaths in the two years before the survey, most of them of women, so no estimate is published. Adult mortality uses the general gradient.
